clue.text: From Malta, I'd thrown out Aussie traveller's bundle of possessions

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters of the two words are tossed around and set down in a new order

parts.note: the contraction I'd gives the letters I and D, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone leaving Malta discards a pile of belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges MALTA plus ID. In Australian folklore a swagman's bedroll and belongings are called his matilda, as in 'Waltzing Matilda'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a swag, the rolled bundle a wandering bushman carries, is known by this woman's name.

clue.text: Hairstyle bringing mocking outcry initially, on china trip?

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it
a trip is a stumble, so the letters of the word tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A haircut draws jeers on a holiday to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes M and O, and 'trip' rearranges CHINA to make HICAN. 'On' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of upstanding hair along an otherwise shaved head is named after a Native American people.

clue.text: City can, encircling an ancient one

indicators.note: encircling says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a can is a tin
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, one city referring back to the definition

explanation.surface: A modern city surrounds an old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encircling' is the container signal. Ur was a Sumerian city in what is now Iraq, and 'one' stands for another city.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern Italian city is the capital of Piedmont, home of the famous Shroud.

clue.text: Bait supplied when a Frenchman rows out after pollock

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first

parts.note: lob is an old English name for the pollack fish

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: An angler lands a pollock and then a Frenchman goes rowing to fetch bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles the Frenchman and the rowing, and 'after' sets that behind the fish. 'pollock' tempts as the painter; lob is an old name for the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: These large earthworms are dug up by anglers for use on hooks.

clue.text: Isn't fit enough to have more than one drink, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is taken as spoken, so it sounds like the plural drink

parts.note: ales are drinks of beer, more than one of them

explanation.surface: Someone too unwell to drink more than one pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives a word that sounds like ALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is unwell or out of sorts suffers, which is the sense here.

clue.text: Passes on knowledge of devilish skills?

parts.note: an imp is a little devil, so devilish points to that mischievous sprite
skills are arts, as in the arts of war

explanation.surface: Someone teaches a course in the black arts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'devilish skills' as the skills of an imp: IMP plus ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on knowledge is to communicate or convey it, a standard sense of the verb.

clue.text: At home, compelling attendance in Sunday school creates rebels

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: attendance in says the word is present inside the other piece

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for Sunday school
something compelling is urgent

explanation.surface: Forcing children to go to Sunday school breeds rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attendance in' is the container signal: the compelling word attends inside the school. SS for Sunday school is a crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: People who rise up against authority are insurrectionists, a synonym.

clue.text: Horse rearing, pleased to be shaking apprentice off

indicators.note: shaking suggests the remaining letters are jumbled
off says one letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: L stands for learner, an apprentice

explanation.surface: A trainee is thrown off a horse that rears up, which pleases it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes L from PLEASED, and 'shaking' rearranges PEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: In dressage this is a movement where the horse raises its forelegs while staying on its hind legs.

clue.text: To propagate, procedure change required

indicators.note: change tells us the order of the letters must be altered

explanation.surface: Breeding requires a change of method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges PROCEDURE. 'required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed or multiply is to produce offspring, a biological synonym.

clue.text: Hobble, needing second hair of the dog!

parts.note: hackles are the hairs on a dog's neck that rise when it is angry

explanation.surface: A hangover cure is needed after a night of drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair of the dog' looks like a hangover cure, a drink taken the morning after; here it is a dog's hackle.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobble is to fetter or restrain, like a chain on the legs of a horse.

clue.text: Wild type of bloomers sported in beer halls

indicators.note: wild here means disordered, so the letters of the fodder run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flaunts outlandish knickers in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like underwear, which 'sported' encourages; it means flowers. 'Wild' rearranges BEER HALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are bell-shaped blue wildflowers, so they are a kind of plant that blooms.

clue.text: Brown as pie can be

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters are able to become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A pie baked until it turns brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges AS PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a reddish-brown pigment, once made from cuttlefish ink, and the colour of old photographs.

clue.text: Large flyer needing entrance, we hear, to study

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning by heart

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for an entrance is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: an entrance is a door

explanation.surface: A big flying creature must be let in to a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns DOOR into a word that sounds the same, DOR. 'Large flyer' suggests an aircraft; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American vulture is among the largest flying birds, with a huge wingspan.

clue.text: Grating on part of canal system causing lack of flow

parts.note: a grating is a grid of bars
a lock is the gated chamber on a canal that raises or lowers boats

explanation.surface: A grating on a canal lock blocks the water.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names traffic jammed so badly that nothing moves, a total halt in movement.

clue.text: Acclamation following pub's modernisation

indicators.note: following places the applause after the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is loud applause

explanation.surface: A pub is cheered for its makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing in new methods or ideas is a kind of updating or renewal.

clue.text: Dope peddler?

parts.note: dope is slang for information or gossip, so someone who peddles dope is a dealer in news rather than drugs

explanation.definitionFit: A gossip who spreads the latest news is a seller of information, which is dope in slang.

clue.text: Wine-lover turned glutton, in America

indicators.note: turned suggests the letters have been turned over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wine buff becomes a greedy guzzler in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges WINE-LOVER. 'Glutton' looks like a greedy person; it is the old European name for this animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This stocky carnivore of northern forests is called the glutton in Europe and by this name in North America.

clue.text: Roofless dwelling by river

indicators.note: roofless says the top of the word is gone, so its first letter is taken off

parts.note: a dwelling is a house

explanation.surface: A house with no roof stands beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roofless' removes the first letter H from HOUSE. The Ouse is a river in England, running through York.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of several English rivers, the best known flowing through York.

clue.text: Flaky complaint from 500 plus getting rough reception

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
plus means and

indicators.note: reception refers to how a word is heard, so the next word is taken by its sound

parts.note: rough is taken here for its sound only

explanation.surface: A complaint about 500 people getting a rough welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reception' gives a word sounding like ROUGH, RUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: This scalp condition sheds small white scales of skin, so it is a flaky ailment.

clue.text: It may be called bread

explanation.definitionFit: A roll call is when a register of names is read out, and a bread roll is a small loaf.

clue.text: Keep finding alien in the showers

indicators.note: in places the alien inside the showers

parts.note: showers are rains
ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film, is the classic alien

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a creature from space in the showers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'finding' is only a link. 'the showers' suggests bathrooms, but means rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something is to hold on to it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: To dispute the proposition, covenanter alters form

indicators.note: alters form says the shape of the word changes, its letters regrouped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who signed a covenant changes position and argues against a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alters form' rearranges COVENANTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To go against or deny a statement is one sense of this verb, besides breaking a rule.

clue.text: Highest and sheer

explanation.definitionFit: Something at the furthest point is utmost, the highest degree; sheer also means utter or total, like utter folly.

clue.text: Thirsty work to right this damaging fungus

parts.note: thirsty means dry

indicators.note: work means knead or rework, so the little word is reshaped

explanation.surface: Fixing a damaging fungus is thirsty work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is the anagram signal, applied to the little word 'to'; 'Thirsty work' tempts as one phrase, but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: This decay of timber is caused by a fungus that turns wood brittle and crumbly.

clue.text: Court exchange producing an irrefutable conclusion

definitions.text: Court exchange producing an irrefutable conclusion

parts.words: Court exchange producing an irrefutable conclusion
parts.note: a tennis court, where a final scoring sequence at six games all settles the set beyond argument

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis this special game decides a set at six games all, so it ends the deadlock definitively.

clue.text: A devotee, having read dictionary's content

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the letters are taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A fan who has studied what is in the dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' takes the letters inside 'reAD DICTionary's'. 'A' and 'having' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen fan of something, a buff or enthusiast, can be called this, like a jazz fiend.

clue.text: In a state secret?

parts.note: a state secret is private or confidential, and something within is the interior or most private part

explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones, and something located inside is interior.

clue.text: A reduced price for passage beyond the horizon?

indicators.note: reduced says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a fare is the price paid for a journey

explanation.surface: A cut-price ticket to a distant destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' takes E off FARE to leave FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something a long way off is distant, perhaps out of sight past the skyline.

clue.text: Even colder here in Paris, monarch found

parts.note: ici is French for here
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen is found in a place even colder than Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Latin initials of Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the comparative of the adjective meaning very cold, more frigid still.

clue.text: Poles supporting pipe when icebound, sway

indicators.note: bound means tied all round, so the ice wraps around the rest
supporting pictures a pole at each end holding up the pipe between them

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north, one of the two poles
a second N, the other pole holding up the far end
a flue is a pipe or duct for smoke

explanation.surface: Frozen up, a pipe is propped on poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' pictures a pole at each end of the pipe, and 'bound' (inside 'icebound') wraps the frozen part around it all; North is the pole used twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway as a noun is power or control over others, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Appease with second small return after taxes

parts.note: wee is Scots for small

indicators.note: return means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: net pay is what is left after taxes

explanation.surface: Someone tries to placate a taxman with a second, smaller tax return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns NET back to front, giving TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to soften or mollify them, which is a figurative sense of this verb.

clue.text: One who decides about new freeway?

definitions.text: One who decides about new freeway?

parts.words: One who decides about new freeway?
parts.note: a planning question is put to an independent person who settles disputes, an arbiter on whether the road goes ahead

explanation.definitionFit: This person arbitrates in disputes or games, judging between two sides.
